I always tell my female clients that "heavy" means something different for everyone. When I started eating carnivore, I weighed 265 pounds and was very out of shape. Even a 5-pound dumbbell felt difficult, and everyday things like bending over or climbing stairs left me exhausted. Now I can comfortably lift 25-pound dumbbells. That might not seem heavy to everyone—my husband can lift much more—but that small increase, along with eating carnivore, completely changed my body. I now weigh 155 pounds.

You don't have to feel exhausted, sore, or miserable when exercising. I have friends who do nothing but roller skate, and they look like athletes. If you can't do a 15-minute bodyweight workout with good form, there's no need to add weights yet. If you're overweight, your body itself is already resistance. People often say "lift heavy," but they don't explain that, so I hope this is helpful. If your goal is maximum muscle growth as quickly as possible, such as for a vacation or competition, then lifting very heavy and training to failure can help. But if your goal is simply to be slim and toned, you don't have to do that. Walking regularly and eating enough protein can naturally help shape your body. I've heard so many carnivore ladies, even the older ladies, say that they slimmed down and got "curvy" but they don't workout at all.

One of my biggest tips for anyone starting carnivore is to use a measuring tape or a waist trainer instead of relying only on the scale. For months, my weight barely changed. Some days I was down five pounds, and the next day I might be up eight pounds, which was frustrating. But I kept tightening my waist trainer and eventually had to buy a smaller size. My husband noticed I felt much smaller, even when I couldn't see the difference myself. At first, the only changes I noticed was that my acne disappeared, and weirdly my nails became stronger and really long. I literally was complaining because I accidently kept scratching us both while sleeping lol. my mood improved. I felt happier, calmer, and less anxious. By the end of the summer, I went shopping for holiday clothes and automatically headed to the plus-size section like I always had. To my surprise, the clothes were too big.
